I completed another targeted continuation across all eight chapters. No scores were assigned.

The repository remained inaccessible for both reading and writing because every shell invocation failed with `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`. Therefore, `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated; the exact ledger dispositions below should be persisted by the parent process.

### 1B — Nuclear responsibility

Accepted:

- `SCU-NUK-E`: FAS Nuclear Notebook 2023 estimates Pakistan’s arsenal at approximately 170 warheads and reports continuing expansion of delivery systems and fissile-material production. This is independent specialist evidence of material exposure, not evidence of a Sharif decision. [FAS Nuclear Notebook](https://fas.org/publication/nuclear-notebook-pakistan-nuclear-weapons-2023/)
- `SCU-NUK-F`: SIPRI’s 2023 nuclear-forces chapter independently places Pakistan among the nuclear-armed states and estimates approximately 170 warheads at the start of 2023. This corroborates exposure and arsenal context, not ruler attribution. [SIPRI Yearbook 2023](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2023/07)
- `SCU-NUK-G`: Pakistan’s 21 March 2023 Conference on Disarmament statement reaffirmed a voluntary pledge not to use or threaten nuclear weapons against non-nuclear states and support for legally binding negative security assurances. This is state-level diplomatic posture, not proof of a Sharif-directed new policy. [UN document CD/2317](https://documents.un.org/access.nsf/get?DS=CD%2F2317&Lang=E&OpenAgent=)
- `SCU-NUK-H`: On 29 August 2023, the IAEA designated Pakistan’s National Institute of Safety and Security as a collaborating centre for nuclear-security education and training. The agreement reflects institutional safety capacity and international cooperation, but does not establish Sharif’s personal intervention. [IAEA](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/pakistan-national-institute-of-safety-and-security-becomes-iaea-collaborating-centre-for-nuclear-security-education-training-and-technical-support)

Disposition change:

- The earlier absence-of-evidence item remains rejected as a source-claim unit and retained only as a gap note.

The chapter now has broader independent exposure and institutional-security evidence, but still lacks a public 2023 NCA decision, independent safety audit, test decision, or ruler-specific command action.

### 2B — International peace and lawful security

Accepted:

- `SCU-INDIA-C`: The PMO stated on 17 January 2023 that Sharif consistently supported resolving Pakistan-India disputes, including Kashmir, through dialogue and peaceful means. This is direct ruler communication, but continuity of established policy rather than a new bilateral outcome. [PMO statement](https://www.radio.gov.pk/17-01-2023/pm-shehbaz-consistently-maintained-that-pakistan-india-must-resolve-issues-through-dialogue-pmo)
- `SCU-INDIA-D`: Sharif’s 19 July 2023 Kashmir statement reaffirmed political, diplomatic, and moral support for Kashmiris and peaceful resolution. It supports diplomatic posture but not a negotiated breakthrough. [Radio Pakistan](https://www.radio.gov.pk/19-07-2023/pm-reiterates-unflinching-support-to-kashmiris-on-day-of-accession-to-pakistan)
- `SCU-INDIA-E`: The March 2023 OIC Contact Group communique records continued diplomatic engagement and references observation of the Line of Control ceasefire. Attribution is institutional and foreign-policy based, not evidence of a personal Sharif decision. [Pakistan Foreign Ministry communique](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/joint-communique-of-the-oic-contact-group-on-jammu-and-kashmir)
- `SCU-IMF-G`: The July 2023 IMF agreement and related bilateral support remain accepted, but the claims are now separated into distinct IMF approval, Saudi deposit, UAE deposit, and Sharif-engagement units rather than one bundled claim.

Contrary/limits:

- No target-period primary source was recovered showing a new India-Pakistan negotiation, ceasefire violation, or Sharif-directed cross-border restraint.
- Kashmir statements establish diplomatic posture, not bilateral results.
- Military operational conduct remains attributed to military institutions unless a federal direction or oversight link is explicit.

### 3B — Domestic safety and protection

Accepted:

- `SCU-3B-FON-001`: Freedom House’s *Freedom on the Net 2023* documents politically motivated censorship, PTA blocking authority, FIA action against journalist Shahid Aslam, and the May disappearance of Imran Riaz Khan. It also records legal challenges and functioning judicial remedies, supplying contrary evidence against an unchecked-repression characterization. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/pakistan/freedom-net/2023)
- `SCU-3B-PTA-001`: Reuters/Dawn reports that mobile broadband was suspended nationwide on 9 May 2023 on Interior Ministry instructions, while major social platforms were restricted. This is direct evidence of federal administrative responsibility for the internet shutdown, distinct from later military-trial decisions. [Dawn/Reuters](https://www.dawn.com/news/1751826/mobile-broadband-suspended-across-country-on-interior-ministrys-instructions-pta)
- `SCU-3B-MILTRIAL-PRIMARY-001`: Pakistan’s Supreme Court’s 23 October 2023 order held that civilians connected to the May 9–10 events should be tried in ordinary criminal courts and declared military proceedings legally ineffective. This is a later judicial corrective record concerning 2023 detention/trial policy, not proof that Sharif personally authorized the military courts. [Supreme Court order](https://www.supremecourt.gov.pk/downloads_judgements/const.p._24_2023_23102023.pdf)
- `SCU-3B-MILTRIAL-PRIMARY-002`: The Supreme Court’s December 2023 suspension of that ruling allowed trials of 103 civilians to continue pending appeal. This preserves the procedural complexity and should not be simplified into a single final legal outcome. [Radio Pakistan](https://www.radio.gov.pk/13-12-2023/sc-suspends-ruling-nullifying-civilians-trials-in-army-courts)

The federal responsibility chain is clearer for the internet shutdown and federal arrest context. It remains incomplete for the operational decision to transfer civilians into military custody and for military command responsibility.

### 4B — Political freedom

Accepted:

- `SCU-4B-ECP-003`: The ECP’s 2023 elections page records consultations with multiple parties and administrative preparations for elections and delimitation. This is evidence of continuing electoral administration and party access, not proof of a fair contest. [ECP elections page](https://ecp.gov.pk/general-elections-2023-2)
- `SCU-4B-ECP-004`: The ECP’s 2023 annual report records that the Council of Common Interests approved the digital census on 5 August 2023, requiring fresh delimitation and contributing to the election delay. [ECP Annual Report 2023](https://ecp.gov.pk/storage/files/3/Annual%20Report-2023%20PPF2-1.pdf)
- `SCU-4B-ECP-005`: The ECP’s August 2023 position stated that fresh delimitation was necessary for accurate representation and fair elections, while acknowledging that the constitutional 90-day period would not be met. [ECP position reported by Dawn](https://www.dawn.com/news/1770933/ecp-defends-move-to-delay-polls-beyond-90-day-limit)
- `SCU-4B-CARETAKER-002`: Sharif and opposition leader Raja Riaz jointly agreed on Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar as caretaker prime minister after dissolution. This establishes an orderly consultation mechanism and succession process. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/anwaar-ul-haq-kakar-nominated-as-caretaker-pm/)

Contrary evidence:

- The ECP’s process evidence mitigates claims of total electoral abandonment.
- The census approval and delayed delimitation nevertheless meant that elections were not held within the ordinary constitutional timetable.
- The practical consequences for opposition access, media independence, and contestability remain only partly documented for the Sharif period.

### 5B — Economic well-being

Accepted:

- `SCU-5B-IMF-STAFF-001`: The IMF staff report records that FY23 BISP spending exceeded FY22 execution by more than 70%, while health and education spending remained below budget. It also describes Kafaalat transfers as low relative to poor-household consumption. [IMF Country Report 23/260](https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/CR/2023/English/1PAKEA2023001.ashx)
- `SCU-5B-IMF-STAFF-002`: The report records that the FY24 budget pursued fiscal consolidation while preserving BISP’s generosity level and establishing monitoring of health and education execution. This separates policy design from actual service delivery.
- `SCU-5B-DISTRIBUTION-001`: The IMF evidence supplies contrary evidence to broad stabilization claims: social protection was expanded, but public-service execution and transfer adequacy remained weak.
- `SCU-5B-INVESTMENT-001`: The IMF report’s FY24 program framework identifies weak investment, constrained fiscal space, and the need for stronger inclusive-growth outcomes. These are structural constraints, not independently attributable Sharif outcomes.

The economic chapter now has better attribution separation: Sharif/federal policy decisions, IMF conditions, BISP execution, and health/education under-execution are distinct. Household-level effects remain incompletely measured.

### 6B — Social well-being and human development

Accepted:

- `SCU-6B-BISP-E-001`: BISP launched Benazir Social Protection Accounts on 7 July 2023, using multiple banks and beneficiary choice of bank to improve payment transparency and autonomy. This is a direct federal program action associated with Sharif’s government. [PID/BISP](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/22993)
- `SCU-6B-BISP-F-001`: BISP reported increased funding from Rs235bn to Rs404.2bn, coverage rising from 7.2m to 9m families, a 25% Kafaalat stipend increase, and expanded education/nutrition programs. These remain official self-reported implementation claims. [PID/BISP](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/22993)
- `SCU-6B-BISP-G-001`: The Economic Survey reported Rs128.9bn in Kafaalat disbursements, assistance to approximately 2.76m flood-affected families, Taleemi Wazaif transfers, and three million enrolled children. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/rs128-9b-disbursed-under-benazir-kafaalat-initiative-from-july-march-fy-2023/)
- `SCU-6B-BISP-H-001`: The IMF independently corroborates BISP expansion, one million newly enrolled Kafaalat families, the 25% stipend increase, and emergency transfers to more than 2.7m flood-affected families. It simultaneously records below-budget health and education spending. [IMF Country Report 23/260](https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/CR/2023/English/1PAKEA2023001.ashx)
- `SCU-6B-EDU-002`: Sharif launched a Rs14bn Pakistan Education Endowment Fund, including Rs3bn for scholarships in the fiscal year, and announced curriculum reforms. [Radio Pakistan](https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-07-2023/pm-launches-pakistan-education-endowment-fund-reforms-in-national-curriculum)
- `SCU-6B-HEALTH-002`: Sharif launched a federal health-insurance program for journalists, media workers, artists, and technical workers, with stated coverage at 1,200 hospitals and an annual limit of Rs1.5m. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-launches-health-program-for-journalists-digitizing-of-federal-laws/)
- `SCU-6B-POLIO-002`: Sharif launched a nationwide January 2023 polio campaign targeting 44.2m children in 156 districts, with WHO and other partners. [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/8720077120dc281ad16d754f6cb97b1d)

Contrary evidence:

- The IMF independently confirms social-protection expansion but also records weak health and education execution and low transfer generosity relative to consumption.
- These units establish federal activity and implementation claims, not uniformly positive human-development outcomes.
- The earlier provincial flood-reconstruction units remain context and must not be relabeled as Sharif-directed federal social policy.

### 7B — Personal integrity

Accepted/disposition changes:

- `SCU-7B-ECP-001`: The ECP maintains a formal 2022–23 asset-and-liabilities disclosure record for parliamentarians. The specific opened declaration for Shehbaz Sharif was not recovered, so this is retained only as an institutional-record lead, not final ruler evidence. [ECP](https://ecp.gov.pk/press-release-regarding-assets-and-liabilities-of-the-parliamentarians-for-the-year-2022-2023)
- `SCU-7B-ECP-002`: ECP confirmed that cabinet members’ asset declarations were submitted under Section 230(3), but the accessible report concerns the caretaker cabinet in November 2023 and is outside Sharif’s elected tenure. Retained as a procedural context item only. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/ecp-dismisses-allegations-of-cabinets-asset-disclosure-refusal/)
- `SCU-7B-ASSET-CANDIDATE-001`: remains rejected/not retained because no direct Sharif declaration was opened.

Existing acquittal and NAB records remain accepted only for the procedural facts they establish. No causal link between Sharif and favorable prosecutorial treatment was recovered. The chapter still lacks direct evidence on recusals, gifts, procurement conflicts, or personal intervention.

### 8B — Effectiveness

Accepted:

- `SCU-8B-IMF-OUTCOME-002`: IMF staff evidence documents actual BISP execution, flood transfers, stipend increases, and enrollment expansion while separately recording weak health and education spending. This is a split implementation/outcome record. [IMF Country Report 23/260](https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/CR/2023/English/1PAKEA2023001.ashx)
- `SCU-8B-SOCIAL-OUTCOME-002`: APP/Economic Survey records federal implementation outputs for BISP, flood assistance, education transfers, and child enrollment. It remains official self-reporting, partially corroborated by the IMF. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/rs128-9b-disbursed-under-benazir-kafaalat-initiative-from-july-march-fy-2023/)
- `SCU-8B-EDUCATION-OUTCOME-001`: The Education Endowment Fund launch establishes a concrete program decision, but no target-period independent evaluation of scholarship outcomes was found.
- `SCU-8B-POLIO-OUTCOME-001`: The nationwide polio campaign establishes implementation and mobilization; no 2023 outcome evaluation attributable to Sharif was recovered.
- `SCU-8B-SUCCESSION-002`: APP records dissolution advice, opposition consultation, and caretaker nomination. This supports orderly succession procedure, while ECP evidence records the subsequent constitutional timing problem. [APP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/anwaarul-haq-kakar-nominated-as-caretaker-pm/)

The effectiveness evidence now distinguishes program, execution, and outcomes more cleanly. Independent evaluation remains limited, especially for macroeconomic stabilization, security policy, education, health, and succession consequences.

- accepted: `SCU-NUK-E`, `SCU-NUK-F`, `SCU-NUK-G`, `SCU-NUK-H`

- accepted: `SCU-3B-FON-001`, `SCU-3B-PTA-001`, `SCU-3B-MILTRIAL-PRIMARY-001`, `SCU-3B-MILTRIAL-PRIMARY-002`
- accepted: `SCU-4B-ECP-003`, `SCU-4B-ECP-004`, `SCU-4B-ECP-005`, `SCU-4B-CARETAKER-002`
- accepted: `SCU-5B-IMF-STAFF-001`, `SCU-5B-IMF-STAFF-002`, `SCU-5B-DISTRIBUTION-001`, `SCU-5B-INVESTMENT-001`
- accepted: `SCU-6B-BISP-E-001`, `SCU-6B-BISP-F-001`, `SCU-6B-BISP-G-001`, `SCU-6B-BISP-H-001`, `SCU-6B-EDU-002`, `SCU-6B-HEALTH-002`, `SCU-6B-POLIO-002`
- retained as context only: `SCU-7B-ECP-001`, `SCU-7B-ECP-002`
- rejected/not retained: `SCU-7B-ASSET-CANDIDATE-001`
- accepted: `SCU-8B-IMF-OUTCOME-002`, `SCU-8B-SOCIAL-OUTCOME-002`, `SCU-8B-EDUCATION-OUTCOME-001`, `SCU-8B-POLIO-OUTCOME-001`, `SCU-8B-SUCCESSION-002`

Research gaps remain in 1B primary NCA decision records, 2B bilateral crisis outcomes, 3B federal authorization of military trials, 7B personal declarations and conflicts, and independent evaluation of 5B/6B/8B outcomes.
